note: A RECORD OF A PARSE, not a result. Merged from the baseline and the re-run, with cc3d3b2a re-anchored to 42001 5.2 by director ruling 2026-09-29. --pinned re-gates from this, no model call.

57042560.key_claim: A new regulation affecting the HR screening AI system is a significant change that triggers AI risk assessment and AI system impact assessment, with documented results retained.
57042560.key_support: The organization shall perform AI risk assessments in accordance with 6.1.2 at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur.

79209585.key_claim: Decisions on continual improvement opportunities and any need for changes to the AIMS are a required output (result) of the management review, not an input.
79209585.key_support: The results of the management review shall include decisions related to continual improvement opportunities and any need for changes to the AI management system.

89837081.key_claim: Conformance is met by documenting the AI system impact assessment results (impacts identified, their evaluation and treatment) in a format the organization judges appropriate for its context, since the standard mandates documentation but not a fixed template.
89837081.key_support: The result of the AI system impact assessment shall be documented.
89837081.cannot_anchor_reason: Partially anchored: the documentation requirement is directly supported by 6.1.4 (and A.5.3, 8.4). The further assertions in the key -- that the documented results must capture impacts, evaluations and how they are addressed, and that the format is left to the organization's context -- are not stated in any supplied passage; the absence of a prescribed template is inferred from silence rather than from an affirmative sentence.

03b9ef69.key_claim: Internal audits must also cover conformity with the organisation's own AIMS requirements and whether the AIMS is effectively implemented and maintained, not just ISO/IEC 42001 requirements.
03b9ef69.key_support: The organization shall conduct internal audits at planned intervals to provide information on whether the AI management system: a) conforms to: 1) the organization’s own requirements for its AI management system; 2) the requirements of this document; b) is effectively implemented and maintained.

04495679.key_claim: The internal audit programme must explicitly consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits.
04495679.key_support: When establishing the internal audit programme(s), the organization shall consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits.

04816f41.key_claim: The deploying organization should require/ensure the supplier delivers appropriate and adequate documentation related to the AI system.
04816f41.key_support: The organization should ensure that the supplier of an AI system delivers appropriate and adequate documentation related to the AI system (see B.6.2.7 and B.8.2).

048b2e4c.key_claim: PDCA in ISO/IEC 42001 is a continual, iterative improvement loop that must be sustained after the AIMS is established, not a one-time project completed at initial deployment or certification.
048b2e4c.key_support: The organization shall establish, implement, maintain, continually improve and document an AI management system, including the processes needed and their interactions, in accordance with the requirements of this document.
048b2e4c.cannot_anchor_reason: Partial anchor only: clause 4.4 (and clause 1) establish the ongoing 'maintain and continually improve' obligation that underlies the key, but none of the supplied passages mentions PDCA or the Plan-Do-Check-Act cycle by name; the explicit PDCA characterization would sit in the standard's Introduction, which is not among the passages.

064f34ac.key_claim: A third-party (externally originated) document deemed necessary for the AIMS must be identified and brought under documented-information control, covering distribution, access and use (including preventing use of obsolete versions).
064f34ac.key_support: Documented information of external origin determined by the organization to be necessary for the planning and operation of the AI management system shall be identified as appropriate and controlled.

077629d1.key_claim: The standard singles out AI systems that update their own parameters in production (continuous learning) because their behaviour can change after deployment, so pre-deployment controls alone are not sufficient and ongoing monitoring is needed.
077629d1.key_support: Where continuous learning is used, the organization should monitor the performance of the AI system to ensure that it continues to meet its design goals and operates on production data as intended.

07a2e32c.key_claim: Under ISO/IEC 42001 the organization must produce an AIMS statement of applicability covering the Annex A (AI-specific) controls, with inclusion/exclusion justified by its AI risk assessment/treatment, rather than relying on its existing ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS SoA.
07a2e32c.key_support: f) produce a statement of applicability that contains the necessary controls [see b), c) and d)] and provide justification for inclusion and exclusion of controls.

07feee65.key_claim: In a combined ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 audit, a single shared management review record may serve as evidence for both standards, provided the auditor verifies that its content satisfies each standard's clause 9.3 requirements.
07feee65.key_support: The certification body may accept documentation that is combined (e.g. for information security, privacy, risk management and quality) as long as the AIMS can be clearly identified together with the appropriate interfaces to the other systems.

097d1896.key_claim: Annex D of ISO/IEC 42001 is informative: it illustrates how the normative clauses apply in sectors such as healthcare but imposes no mandatory requirements.
097d1896.cannot_anchor_reason: No supplied passage states the normative status of Annex D. The supplied D.1 text only says the management system is applicable to any organization and lists example sectors (including health); it never characterizes Annex D as informative, non-mandatory, or as adding no requirements. The '(informative)' designation of Annex D appears in the annex heading/foreword of ISO/IEC 42001, which is not among the supplied passages, so the key cannot be anchored verbatim here.

09ae6e83.key_claim: A hospital that acquires an AI diagnostic tool from an external vendor and uses it occupies the AI customer (AI user) role in relation to that vendor.
09ae6e83.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 22989 — clause 4.1 only enumerates the roles and states that "A detailed description of these roles is provided by ISO/IEC 22989"; the definitional criteria that distinguish AI customer from AI provider, AI producer and AI partner (i.e. that acquiring and using a supplied AI system makes an organization a customer) are in that unheld document.

09db140e.key_claim: An internal AIMS audit belongs to the 'Check' phase of PDCA because it is a performance evaluation mechanism that monitors the AIMS against its requirements.
09db140e.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 Clause 9 (Performance evaluation), specifically 9.2 Internal audit, and any PDCA-cycle mapping text (e.g. Introduction) — none of these clauses are among the supplied passages.
09db140e.cannot_anchor_reason: No supplied passage mentions internal audit, performance evaluation, or the Plan-Do-Check-Act phases. The supplied passages cover general scope, definitions, AIMS establishment (4.4), continual improvement (10.1), Annex A/D guidance and certification-body scope documents, none of which place internal audit in the 'Check' phase.

0be22fbf.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 specifies requirements for a management system by which an organization responsibly develops, provides or uses AI systems, rather than technical or product requirements.
0be22fbf.key_support: This document specifies the requirements and provides guidance for establishing, implementing, maintaining and continually improving an AI (artificial intelligence) management system within the context of an organization.

0cbb853c.key_claim: The ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A data-provenance control requires documenting where the data used in AI systems came from over its life cycle, which is a different risk object from an access-control procedure governing who reaches the system, so one cannot serve as evidence for the other.
0cbb853c.key_support: Data provenance The organization shall define and document a process for recording the provenance of data used in its AI systems over the life cycles of the data and the AI system.

0ccaffdc.key_claim: The statement of applicability must reflect the organization's current risks and controls, so changes such as newly deployed AI systems that affect control applicability require the SoA to be updated.
0ccaffdc.key_support: All identified risks and the risk management measures (controls) established to address them shall be reflected in the statement of applicability.

0e74fc58.key_claim: Conformance authority is the assigned responsibility for ensuring the AI management system meets the standard's requirements, whereas internal audit is a distinct, separate verification activity (and need not be held by the same person).
0e74fc58.key_support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the AI management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management.
0e74fc58.rests_on_unheld_source: The 'internal audit is a separate verification activity' half of the key is not covered by any supplied passage; it rests on ISO/IEC 42001 clause 9.2 (internal audit), which is not among the passages, and on ISO 19011 audit practice as cited in the explanation.

0f002bf0.key_claim: When a harmful AI output occurs and the investigation is still ongoing, the organization should activate its documented incident communication plan and notify relevant stakeholders rather than waiting for the investigation to conclude.
0f002bf0.key_support: The organization shall determine and document a plan for communicating incidents to users of the AI system.

1080ad8f.key_claim: Evidence of effectiveness must show the corrective action was implemented and that its root cause no longer produces the nonconformity, i.e. a review of effectiveness rather than mere completion of steps.
1080ad8f.key_support: d) review the effectiveness of any corrective action taken;

1105cbdc.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 requires the AI policy to be reviewed at planned intervals (or as needed) to keep it suitable, adequate and effective, so a one-time approval is insufficient.
1105cbdc.key_support: Review of the AI policy The AI policy shall be reviewed at planned intervals or additionally as needed to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.

113fc289.key_claim: Confirming that the architecture conforms to written specifications (verification) does not discharge the requirement for validation; separate validation measures must still be defined, applied and evaluated against criteria to confirm fitness for intended use.
113fc289.key_support: The organization shall define and document verification tion and validation measures for the AI system and specify criteria for their use.

121f8e71.key_claim: Competence records from information security cannot by themselves demonstrate the competence needed for AI management; ISO/IEC 42001 requires the organization to determine and evidence competence specific to work affecting its AI performance.
121f8e71.key_support: determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance

1253931b.key_claim: The organization must still control the externally provided bias-detection process; responsibility for the AI management system remains with the organization regardless of the supplier's own ISO/IEC 42001 certification.
1253931b.key_support: The organization shall ensure that externally provided processes, products or services that are relevant to the AI management system are controlled.

144ef67c.key_claim: The AI policy supplies the framework and high-level commitments, while the separate measurable target ('reduce AI-related bias incidents by 15% within 12 months') is an AI objective derived from and consistent with that policy — the standard treats them as distinct artifacts.
144ef67c.key_support: b) provides a framework for setting AI objectives (see 6.2);

145fa273.key_claim: The infrastructure-based scope may be too narrow, because an AIMS boundary drawn only by where systems are hosted can omit AI the organisation actually uses in its activities.
145fa273.key_support: When determining this scope, the organization shall consider: — the external and internal issues referred to in 4.1; — the requirements referred to in 4.2.

152a64ac.key_claim: The organisation must apply AI system life cycle controls across all stages it governs (deployment, operation, retirement) even for an AI system built by a third party, rather than limiting or exempting them because it did not develop the system.
152a64ac.cannot_anchor_reason: None of the supplied passages states that the A.6 life cycle controls apply irrespective of who developed the system, nor that an acquiring/deploying organisation must apply them across the stages it governs (deployment, operation, retirement) and cannot rely on the developer's documentation. The supplied A.6.1/A.6.2 controls and their B.6 guidance are written for design, development, deployment, operation, documentation and logging without addressing role-based applicability (developer vs. deployer/user), and the A.5/B.5 and 6.1.4/8.4 passages concern impact assessment only. The closest wording ('Support for the system can be internal, external or both, depending on the needs of the organization and how the system was acquired' in B.6.2.6, and 'development, provision or use of AI systems' in 6.1.4) concerns support arrangements and impact assessment scope, not the scope of life cycle controls for acquired third-party systems; the provisions that would carry this key (e.g. the standard's scope/applicability and third-party relationship controls) are not among the supplied passages.

15cb90ee.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 Annex A is a required reference control set that the organisation must address control-by-control in a Statement of Applicability, justifying any exclusions.
15cb90ee.cannot_anchor_reason: No supplied passage states the Statement of Applicability requirement or the duty to justify exclusion of Annex A controls. That requirement sits in ISO/IEC 42001 clause 6.1.3 (AI risk treatment), which was not provided. The closest supplied text, clause 8.1, only requires implementation of 'the controls determined according to 6.1.3' and notes that 'Annex A lists reference controls and Annex B provides implementation guidance for them' — it says nothing about an SoA, comprehensive consideration of all Annex A controls, or justification of exclusions. Clauses D.1/D.2 address integration with other management system standards but do not make any claim about Annex A applicability, so the distractors about integration cannot be resolved from the held passages either.

17b183f2.key_claim: The agenda omits two required management review inputs: the status of actions from previous management reviews and changes in external and internal issues relevant to the AIMS.
17b183f2.key_support: The management review shall include: a) the status of actions from previous management reviews; b) changes in external and internal issues that are relevant to the AI management system;

17b73169.key_claim: Top management must assign responsibility and authority for two functions: ensuring the AI management system conforms to the standard's requirements, and reporting on AIMS performance to top management.
17b73169.key_support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the AI management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management.

1ac02db3.key_claim: The organization must establish and operate an internal process allowing staff to proactively report concerns about the organization's role with respect to an AI system.
1ac02db3.key_support: Reporting of concerns The organization shall define and put in place a process to report concerns about the organization’s role with respect to an AI system throughout its life cycle.

1ad52afa.key_claim: When a new national AI regulation is enacted after the initial context determination, the organization must review and update its clause 4.1 context determination, because determining relevant external and internal issues (including applicable legal requirements) is a continuing requirement rather than a one-time exercise.
1ad52afa.key_support: The organization shall determine external and internal issues that are relevant to its purpose and that affect its ability to achieve the intended result(s) of its AI management system.

1b0d5be6.key_claim: A static model's accuracy can degrade because of shifting data, so AI system life cycle obligations (notably monitoring) continue into the operation stage after deployment.
1b0d5be6.key_support: At the minimum, this should include system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support.

1ce517bd.key_claim: The comparison of selected controls against Annex A serves to verify that no necessary controls have been omitted and to identify whether additional controls beyond Annex A are required.
1ce517bd.key_support: b) determine all controls that are necessary to implement the AI risk treatment options chosen and compare the controls with those in Annex A to verify that no necessary controls have been omitted;

20ad8d94.key_claim: A supplier-provided model card can be treated as potentially sufficient documentation if it is appropriate and adequate to support the organization's own risk assessment and responsible-AI approach, since no fixed document list (training data, weights) is mandated.
20ad8d94.key_support: The organization should ensure that the supplier of an AI system delivers appropriate and adequate documentation related to the AI system (see B.6.2.7 and B.8.2).

23fdd105.key_claim: Omitting changes in external and internal issues from a management review is incorrect, because ISO/IEC 42001 makes such changes a mandatory input to every management review rather than a one-time establishment activity.
23fdd105.key_support: b) changes in external and internal issues that are relevant to the AI management system;

24172f5a.key_claim: Where a sole auditor on a combined ISO/IEC 27001 + ISO/IEC 42001 audit lacks AI-specific competence, the gap must be closed before or during the audit (e.g. by adding a technically competent expert to the team) rather than merely noted afterwards.
24172f5a.key_support: The certification body shall have a process for selecting and appointing the audit team, including the audit team leader and technical experts as necessary, taking into account the competence needed to achieve the objectives of the audit and requirements for impartiality.

24177d84.key_claim: Audit scope and audit criteria are distinct elements of an internal audit: scope sets the boundaries of what the audit covers, while criteria are the requirements against which conformity is assessed.
24177d84.key_support: define the audit objectives, criteria and scope for each audit
24177d84.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO 19011 (cited in Note 3 to entry of 3.18 as the source of the definitions of "audit evidence" and "audit criteria"; the substantive definitions of audit scope and audit criteria are not reproduced in the supplied passages)

255323d0.key_claim: Assigning both the AIMS-conformance authority and the AIMS-performance-reporting authority to a single person is permissible, because ISO/IEC 42001 lists them as two distinct assigned authorities without requiring that different individuals hold them.
255323d0.key_support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the AI management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management.
255323d0.cannot_anchor_reason: The quoted clause anchors the two authorities as distinct items that must be assigned; the further part of the key (that no separation of holders is required) rests on the absence of any separation or conflict-of-interest requirement in the supplied passages rather than on positive wording.

25b70532.key_claim: Integrated implementation of ISO/IEC 42001 alongside ISO 9001 and ISO/IEC 27001 is facilitated by the shared (harmonised/high-level) structure, but joint certification is not mandatory — maintaining separate certifications remains compliant.
25b70532.key_support: Given that both ISO/IEC 27001 and the AI management systems use the high-level structure, their integrated use is facilitated and of great benefit for the organization.

26d79fe7.key_claim: A valid ISO/IEC 42001 certificate demonstrates that the organization's AI management system conforms to the requirements of ISO/IEC 42001 (evidencing responsible governance of its AI systems), and nothing more — it does not certify products/services or establish legal compliance.
26d79fe7.key_support: operates in compliance with the requirements of ISO/IEC 42001:2023

271bf759.key_claim: Adding the missing review step, on its own, is a correction — it fixes the detected nonconformity without investigating or eliminating its cause — and therefore is not yet a corrective action.
271bf759.key_support: a) react to the nonconformity and as applicable: 1) take action to control and correct it; 2) deal with the consequences; b) evaluate the need for action to eliminate the cause(s) of the nonconformity, so that it does not recur or occur elsewhere

27f32165.key_claim: Reviewing AI incident response times against the organization's stated objective is a 'Check' phase activity — i.e. monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation of AIMS performance against its objectives.
27f32165.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 42001 Clause 9 (Performance evaluation), in particular 9.1 Monitoring, measurement, analysis and evaluation, and the PDCA/Plan-Do-Check-Act framing in the Introduction — none of which are among the supplied passages.
27f32165.cannot_anchor_reason: No supplied passage addresses performance evaluation, monitoring/measurement against objectives, or the Plan-Do-Check-Act phases. The supplied passages cover the AIMS scope and definition (1, 3.1, 3.4, 3.5, 3.6, 3.8, 4.4), continual improvement (10.1), Annex A/D guidance, and certification-body requirements (ISO/IEC 17021-1, ISO/IEC 42006) — none of which state that measuring results against stated objectives constitutes a 'Check' activity.

288b92d5.key_claim: A single management review record may serve both ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 clause 9.3, but an information security risk assessment cannot be used in place of the AI-specific risk assessment required by ISO/IEC 42001.
288b92d5.key_support: The organization shall define and establish an AI risk assessment process that: a) is informed by and aligned with the AI policy (see 5.2) and AI objectives (see 6.2);

29b73430.key_claim: The correct response to a human-competency gap is to identify and document the human resources and their competences needed for the AI system's life-cycle activities, ensuring they are available.
29b73430.key_support: Human resources As part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about the human resources and their competences utilized for the development, deployment, operation, change management, maintenance, transfer and decommissioning, as well as verification and integration of the AI system.

2a6b35ac.key_claim: The ISMS awareness delivery mechanisms may be reused, but the awareness content must be extended to cover AI-specific matters (AI policy, AI impacts, responsible use) because ISO/IEC 42001 Clause 7.3 requires awareness of the AI policy and of contribution to the AI management system, which security content does not cover.
2a6b35ac.key_support: Persons doing work under the organization’s control shall be aware of: — the AI policy (see 5.2); — their contribution to the effectiveness of the AI management system, including the benefits of improved AI performance; — the implications of not conforming with the AI management system requirements.

2b69401f.key_claim: Meeting minutes that serve as evidence of AIMS activities count as documented information and therefore must be controlled under ISO/IEC 42001, regardless of their informal format.
2b69401f.key_support: Documented information required by the AI management system and by this document shall be controlled to ensure: a) it is available and suitable for use, where and when it is needed; b) it is adequately protected (e.g. from loss of confidentiality, improper use or loss of integrity).

2b85823e.key_claim: Omitting changes in interested party needs and expectations from the management review is a gap, because ISO/IEC 42001 lists it as a required management review input.
2b85823e.key_support: c) changes in needs and expectations of interested parties that are relevant to the AI management system;

2d291853.key_claim: Fulfilling Annex A responsible-use requirements means defining responsible-use objectives and establishing documented processes that ensure the AI system is actually used in accordance with its intended use and accompanying documentation.
2d291853.key_support: The organization shall ensure that the AI system is used according to the intended uses of the AI system and its accompanying documentation.

2e37975a.key_claim: The organization should repeat the AI risk assessment because significant changes to the AI system (retraining on an expanded dataset) can introduce new or altered risks.
2e37975a.key_support: The organization shall perform AI risk assessments in accordance with 6.1.2 at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur.

31b6119c.key_claim: Contractually transferring liability for a third-party AI model's outputs is a valid action because risk transfer is one of the recognized AI risk treatment options, alongside avoidance, modification and acceptance.
31b6119c.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO 31000 (and ISO/IEC 27005), which is where the enumeration of risk treatment options as avoidance, modification/mitigation, sharing/transfer and retention/acceptance is set out; it is not among the supplied passages.
31b6119c.cannot_anchor_reason: The supplied passages require the organization to 'select appropriate AI risk treatment options' (6.1.3 a)) but nowhere enumerate or name the options, and in particular never mention transfer, avoidance, modification or acceptance. Clause 3.26 and 6.1.3 concern controls, the statement of applicability and the risk treatment plan only. No supplied sentence states that risk transfer is a recognized treatment option, so the key cannot be anchored without stretching 'appropriate AI risk treatment options' beyond what the text says.

332c147a.key_claim: Annex A's controls are a reference set for meeting objectives and addressing risks, so an organization need not implement every listed control.
332c147a.key_support: Not all the control objectives and controls listed in Table A.1 are required to be used, and the organization can design and implement their own controls (see 6.1.3).

3619a258.key_claim: Awareness under ISO/IEC 42001 is not satisfied by policy recall alone because it must also cover the implications/consequences of not conforming with AI management system requirements.
3619a258.key_support: Persons doing work under the organization’s control shall be aware of: — the AI policy (see 5.2); — their contribution to the effectiveness of the AI management system, including the benefits of improved AI performance; — the implications of not conforming with the AI management system requirements.

362a3bab.key_claim: Annex D of ISO/IEC 42001 identifies ISO/IEC 27001 (information security management) as the management system standard most closely integrated with an AI management system, because AI governance and information security share closely related requirements and risks.
362a3bab.key_support: Given that both ISO/IEC 27001 and the AI management systems use the high-level structure, their integrated use is facilitated and of great benefit for the organization.

379b53fe.key_claim: Following significant expansion of the AI portfolio, the organization should reassess the adequacy of the full range of AI system resources — human resources/competences, tooling, and system/computing infrastructure — rather than treating the original assessment as sufficient or limiting review to one resource type.
379b53fe.key_support: The organization shall identify and document relevant resources required for the activities at given AI system life cycle stages and other AI-related activities relevant for the organization.
379b53fe.cannot_anchor_reason: Partial anchor: A.4.2 (with A.4.3–A.4.6) supports the breadth of resources in scope (human resources, tooling, data, system and computing resources), and A.4's objective requires accounting for resources 'in order to fully understand and address risks and impacts'. However, none of the supplied A.4 passages state an explicit requirement to re-perform or update the resource assessment at intervals or upon change; the only supplied 'review at planned intervals' wording is A.2.4, which applies to the AI policy, not to resources.

388b7724.key_claim: An updated externally-originated regulatory guidance document determined necessary for the AIMS must be identified and brought under documented-information control (including version control so the superseded version is not still used).
388b7724.key_support: Documented information of external origin determined by the organization to be necessary for the planning and operation of the AI management system shall be identified as appropriate and controlled.

3996f5d4.key_claim: Rejected loan applicants must be counted among the bank's AIMS interested parties because they can perceive themselves as affected by the AI-driven decisions.
3996f5d4.key_support: person or organization (3.1) that can affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a decision or activity

3dc72015.key_claim: Beyond generic quality/security controls, the organization must apply AI-specific supplier requirements that are scaled to the type of supplier and the risk posed, covering matters such as bias, transparency, and intended-use documentation.
3dc72015.key_support: Organizations should consider different types of suppliers, what they supply, and the varying level of risk this can pose to the system and organization as a whole in determining the selection of suppliers, the requirements placed on those suppliers, and the levels of ongoing monitoring and evaluation needed for the suppliers.

3ddabce2.key_claim: The existing ISO/IEC 27001 document-control procedure can be reused in form for the AIMS, but must be re-examined to confirm it adequately controls AI-management-system documented information.
3ddabce2.key_support: Documented information required by the AI management system and by this document shall be controlled to ensure: a) it is available and suitable for use, where and when it is needed; b) it is adequately protected (e.g. from loss of confidentiality, improper use or loss of integrity).
3ddabce2.cannot_anchor_reason: Partial anchor only: 7.5.3 establishes that AI management system documented information must itself be controlled (so an inherited ISMS procedure must be confirmed to cover it), and D.2 endorses integrated use of ISO/IEC 27001 with the AI management system. No supplied passage states explicitly that an existing procedure must be 're-examined'; that step is inferred from the 7.5.3 obligation.

3e1dc277.key_claim: The status of actions from previous management reviews is a mandatory management review input under ISO/IEC 42001, so it cannot be omitted on the grounds that those actions are tracked elsewhere.
3e1dc277.key_support: The management review shall include: a) the status of actions from previous management reviews;

3e8a2825.key_claim: The AIMS owner should determine what information users need and provide it by whatever delivery method or combination actually gets it to users, since the standard prescribes no specific channel.
3e8a2825.key_support: System documentation and inforThe organization shall determine and provide the necesmation for users sary information to users of the AI system.
3e8a2825.rests_on_unheld_source: GDPR (referenced in distractor B and the explanation) is not among the supplied passages

3fbd1080.key_claim: For a procurement manager whose work affects AI performance, the organization must determine the competence needed, take action to close any gap, and keep documented evidence.
3fbd1080.key_support: The organization shall: — determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance; — ensure that these persons are competent on the basis of appropriate education, training or experience; — where applicable, take actions to acquire the necessary competence, and evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken.

40820cfe.key_claim: The B.9.3 list (fairness, transparency, human oversight, etc.) is illustrative 'should' guidance, from which the implementer selects and applies considerations relevant to its own context and risk.
40820cfe.key_support: Depending on its context, the organization should identify its objectives related to responsible use.

423162b7.key_claim: No prior formal integration (or existing certification) is needed for an organisation running both ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO/IEC 42001 to share a single audit programme and management review cycle, but the audit criteria of each standard must be kept distinct rather than merged into one unified criterion set.
423162b7.cannot_anchor_reason: Neither supplied passage states the two operative propositions of the key. D.2 only says that integrated use of ISO/IEC 27001 and the AI management system 'is facilitated' and that controls 'can be integrated' — it says nothing about audit programmes, management review cycles, prerequisites of formal system merger, or certification status. Clause 9.2.2 a) requires the organization to 'define the audit objectives, criteria and scope for each audit', which is a per-audit definition requirement; it does not assert that each standard's audit criteria must remain distinct or prohibit a unified criterion set across two standards. The distinct-criteria prohibition and the 'no prior integration required' permission are both inferences beyond the supplied text.

42c1833c.key_claim: The awareness procedure's structure/form may carry over from ISO/IEC 27001, but its content must be revised so that awareness covers AI-specific subject matter (AI policy, AI performance, AI management system requirements) rather than information security topics.
42c1833c.key_support: Persons doing work under the organization’s control shall be aware of: — the AI policy (see 5.2); — their contribution to the effectiveness of the AI management system, including the benefits of improved AI performance; — the implications of not conforming with the AI management system requirements.

430a65d2.key_claim: Under ISO/IEC 42001's third-party and customer controls, the AI provider should address the bank as a relevant third party/customer and allocate AI system life cycle responsibilities between itself and the bank.
430a65d2.key_support: Allocating responsibilities The organization shall ensure that responsibilities within their AI system life cycle are allocated between the organization, its partners, suppliers, customers and third parties.
430a65d2.cannot_anchor_reason: The 'allocate life-cycle responsibilities between both parties' half of the key is anchored verbatim in A.10.2 (with A.10.4 confirming customers are in scope). ea7c3ae6.cannot_anchor_reason: The supplied passages (A.1, B.1, 6.1.3) describe only the purpose and use of Annex A/Annex B controls — that Table A.1 provides reference controls, that not all need be used, and how they feed the statement of applicability. None of the supplied text reproduces Table A.1's category headings or its A.2–A.10 numbering, and none states or implies any relationship (or absence of relationship) between Annex A categories and main-body clauses 4–10. The body of Table A.1 itself, which would be needed to verify the numbering and thematic organization, was not provided.

ec233801.key_claim: The AI policy's role is to provide a framework for setting AI objectives, while the measurable AI objectives themselves are established under a separate clause (6.2), so the policy need not list numerical KPIs.
ec233801.key_support: b) provides a framework for setting AI objectives (see 6.2);

ed3dbc84.key_claim: The arrangement is non-compliant because ISO/IEC 42001 requires documented information evidencing the management review — the inputs considered and the results reached — not merely a list of final decisions.
ed3dbc84.key_support: Documented information shall be available as evidence of the results of management reviews.

edb3330c.key_claim: Using auditors who hold only ISO/IEC 27001 competence for a combined internal audit programme is insufficient, because auditing an AI management system requires AI-specific competence beyond ISO/IEC 27001 knowledge.
edb3330c.key_support: determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance

edb840b2.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001's consistency requirement is satisfied by a documented, uniformly applied risk assessment process yielding comparable results, not by assessors producing identical numerical scores.
edb840b2.key_support: b) is designed such that repeated AI risk assessments can produce consistent, valid and comparable results;

ee7e18ea.key_claim: The auditor is right: the Statement of Applicability is only documentation of which controls are necessary and why, so separate objective evidence is needed to show a control is actually implemented and operating.
ee7e18ea.key_support: The organization shall implement the AI risk treatment plan according to 6.1.3 and verify its effectiveness.

f0075905.key_claim: The nurses' bypassing of alert thresholds must be evaluated as foreseeable misuse, with potential patient harm assessed and documented within the AI system impact assessment.
f0075905.key_support: The AI system impact assessment shall determine the potential consequences an AI system’s deployment, intended use and foreseeable misuse has on individuals or groups of individuals, or both, and societies.

f073235b.key_claim: Because the same supplier nonconformity recurred, the organisation must treat the earlier corrective action as ineffective and redo the cause analysis and implement new action.
f073235b.key_support: b) evaluate the need for action to eliminate the cause(s) of the nonconformity, so that it does not recur or occur elsewhere, by: 1) reviewing the nonconformity; 2) determining the causes of the nonconformity; 3) determining if similar nonconformities exist or can potentially occur; c) implement any action needed; d) review the effectiveness of any corrective action taken;

f1f9cc78.key_claim: When direct access to the impact assessment is restricted, the auditor should exercise professional judgement and evaluate whether the summary, the executive declaration and other corroborating evidence together constitute a sufficient objective basis to reach an audit conclusion on that requirement.
f1f9cc78.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO 19011 clauses on collecting and verifying information, generating audit findings and reaching audit conclusions (e.g. 6.4.7, 6.4.8, 6.4.9) and A.6 on sampling — these specific clauses are not among the supplied ISO 19011 extracts.
f1f9cc78.cannot_anchor_reason: No supplied passage addresses what an auditor does when direct access to evidence is restricted, nor the sufficiency of alternative/corroborating evidence as a basis for an audit conclusion. The nearest supplied text, ISO/IEC 42001 3.18 ('systematic and independent process (3.8) for obtaining evidence and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which the audit criteria are fulfilled'), is an informative definition of 'audit' and does not speak to sufficiency of evidence or restricted access; ISO 19011 5.6 e) mentions 'sufficiency and adequacy of documented information in the audit process' only as an audit-programme monitoring input, not as an auditor's judgement on forming a conclusion. Anchoring the key in either would be a stretch.

f2265782.key_claim: The reviewer is wrong: the AI policy is required only to state high-level commitments and provide a framework for setting objectives, while measurable/numeric targets are a feature of AI objectives, not of the policy.
f2265782.key_support: Top management shall establish an AI policy that: a) is appropriate to the purpose of the organization; b) provides a framework for setting AI objectives (see 6.2); c) includes a commitment to meet applicable requirements; d) includes a commitment to continual improvement of the AI management system.

f34d03f6.key_claim: Because data drift can degrade even a static, non-self-updating model, ISO/IEC 42001 life cycle obligations continue into the operation stage, requiring ongoing performance monitoring after deployment.
f34d03f6.key_support: At the minimum, this should include system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support.
f34d03f6.cannot_anchor_reason: Partial anchor only: A.6.2.6 (with C.3.6, 'Sources of risk can appear over the entire AI system life cycle') supports that life cycle obligations extend into ongoing operation and performance monitoring, but no supplied passage uses or defines the concept of data/concept drift degrading a static model; that part of the key is inference from the standard's life cycle framing rather than quoted text.

f50f74e8.key_claim: Clause 4.1 requires the organization to determine whether climate change is a relevant issue irrespective of whether it operates or is certified to an environmental management system such as ISO 14001.
f50f74e8.key_support: The organization shall determine whether climate change is a relevant issue.

f582abc4.key_claim: In the PDCA cycle as applied to an AI management system, the 'Plan' phase comprises establishing the AIMS scope, the organization's context, risk assessment, AI objectives and governing policies.
f582abc4.cannot_anchor_reason: None of the supplied passages describes the PDCA cycle or allocates activities (scope, context, risk assessment, objectives, policies) to a 'Plan' phase. Clause 1 and 4.4 only require establishing/implementing/maintaining/continually improving the AIMS, 10.1 covers continual improvement, and 3.4/3.5/3.6 are definitions; the PDCA breakdown appears in the ISO/IEC 42001 Introduction and Clauses 4-6, which were not supplied.

f6672984.key_claim: Clause 6.1.4 requires the organization to consider the AI system impact assessment results as an input to the risk assessment, so results documented afterwards and not used to adjust risk ratings violate that obligation.
f6672984.key_support: The organization shall consider the results of the AI system impact assessment in the risk assessment (see 6.1.2).

f74447c0.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 obliges the organization to determine, for AIMS-relevant external (and internal) communications, what it will communicate, when, with whom, and how.
f74447c0.key_support: The organization shall determine the internal and external communications relevant to the AI management system including: — what it will communicate; — when to communicate; — with whom to communicate; — how to communicate.

f75f5026.key_claim: The competence requirement is not limited to developers or operators: the organization must determine competence for any person doing work under its control that affects AI performance, which includes a procurement manager selecting AI vendors.
f75f5026.key_support: determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance

f7eb23b7.key_claim: AI subjects are the individuals affected by or exposed to an AI system's outputs, whereas AI customers are the entities that acquire or use AI products or services.
f7eb23b7.rests_on_unheld_source: ISO/IEC 22989 (the role definitions for 'AI subject' and 'AI customer'; clause 4.1 states 'A detailed description of these roles is provided by ISO/IEC 22989.')
f7eb23b7.cannot_anchor_reason: Clause 4.1 only enumerates the roles ('AI customers, including AI users' and 'AI subjects, including data subjects and other subjects') without defining them, and expressly defers the detailed descriptions to ISO/IEC 22989, which is not among the supplied passages. No supplied passage states that AI subjects are individuals affected by a system's outputs or that AI customers are entities that acquire or use AI products or services; clause 3.2 defines 'interested party' generally, not the AI subject role.

fa5276a3.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42001 is the standard that specifies the AIMS requirements an organization implements, while conformity assessment (certification) is carried out by independent third-party certification bodies operating under accreditation criteria.
fa5276a3.key_support: Certification of AIMS is a third-party conformity assessment activity (as described in ISO/IEC 17000:2020, 4.5), and bodies performing this activity are third-party conformity assessment bodies.

fa7bfe7d.key_claim: The existing ISO/IEC 27001 document control procedure can be reused in form for the AIMS, but its scope must first be reviewed to ensure it covers the documented information the AI management system requires.
fa7bfe7d.key_support: The organization’s AI management system shall include: a) documented information required by this document; b) documented information determined by the organization as being necessary for the effectiveness of the AI management system.
fa7bfe7d.cannot_anchor_reason: Partial anchor only: 7.5.1 establishes that the AIMS must encompass AI-specific documented information (so scope must be checked), and D.2 supports integrated use of ISO/IEC 27001 with the AIMS ('their integrated use is facilitated and of great benefit for the organization'). No supplied passage states in terms that an inherited procedure must be reviewed before adoption; the key is inferred from the combination.

fcb8a516.key_claim: ISO/IEC 42006 sets requirements for the bodies that audit and certify AI management systems, whereas ISO/IEC 42001 sets the AIMS requirements that organizations themselves implement.
fcb8a516.key_support: The requirements contained in this document, when implemented, support the demonstration of competence, consistency and reliability by the bodies performing auditing and certification of an artificial intelligence management system (AIMS) according to ISO/IEC 42001 for organizations that provide, develop or use AI systems.

fce10a55.key_claim: The organization should determine the necessary competence, identify the gap in AI ethics/legal/societal expertise, and take action (training, hiring or contracting) to acquire the missing competence.
fce10a55.key_support: The organization shall: — determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance; — ensure that these persons are competent on the basis of appropriate education, training or experience; — where applicable, take actions to acquire the necessary competence, and evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken.

fd29a029.key_claim: An organization may use/integrate its existing ISO 27001 document control procedure to control AIMS documented information, as long as that integrated procedure satisfies all ISO/IEC 42001 documented information requirements.
fd29a029.cannot_anchor_reason: No supplied passage addresses integration or sharing of procedures across management systems. Clause 7.5.3 states only what must be ensured and addressed for AIMS documented information ('Documented information required by the AI management system and by this document shall be controlled to ensure...'); it is silent on whether a procedure maintained for another management system (e.g. ISO/IEC 27001) may be reused. The key's operative assertion — that integration is permitted — rests on the absence of a prohibition rather than on any sentence in the held passages, and the comparison with ISO/IEC 27001 requirements would require that standard, which is not supplied.

fd625faf.key_claim: The management review is a top-management activity conducted at planned intervals to assess the AIMS's continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.
fd625faf.key_support: Top management shall review the organization’s AI management system, at planned intervals, to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness.

fdc45841.key_claim: The authority assigned under ISO/IEC 42001 for performance reporting is the duty to report/communicate AI management system performance to top management.
fdc45841.key_support: Top management shall assign the responsibility and authority for: a) ensuring that the AI management system conforms to the requirements of this document; b) reporting on the performance of the AI management system to top management.

ffaa8a5f.key_claim: Under ISO/IEC 42001, risk identification and risk evaluation must remain distinct activities because the AI risk assessment process requires separately identifying risks and evaluating them against established risk criteria.
ffaa8a5f.key_support: c) identifies risks that aid or prevent achieving its AI objectives; d) analyses the AI risks to: 1) assess the potential consequences to the organization, individuals and societies that would result if the identified risks were to materialize; 2) assess, where applicable, the realistic likelihood of the identified risks; 3) determine the levels of risk; e) evaluates the AI risks to: 1) compare the results of the risk analysis with the risk criteria (see 6.1.1); 2) prioritize the assessed risks for risk treatment.
